title: Commission rules — LIF caps, clawback and consent
product: Corporations Act 2001 s963B–s963BB and ASIC Corporations (Life Insurance Commissions) Instrument 2017/510
version: Rule guide FY2026-27 v1.0 — current at 23 Nov 2026
summary: How commission on life risk insurance is capped and clawed back under the Life Insurance Framework (LIF), the informed-consent rule for commission that applies to insurance issued or sold from 9 Jul 2025, and how Life Advice Guru shows commission in dollars. The SoA Drafting assistant uses it to disclose commission; Theo's file audits check it.
rules:
1 When commission is allowed — commission on life risk insurance isn't conflicted remuneration if either the benefit ratio is the same in the first year and every later year (level commission), or it meets the benefit-ratio and clawback requirements set under s963BA (s963B(1)(b)). Either way, the client's informed consent is also required (s963BB). Commission on group super policies and on default cover in super is still conflicted remuneration (s963B(2)).
2 Benefit ratio — the commission divided by the policy cost; the policy cost is the premiums plus fees and instalment fees (s963B(3A)–(3B)).
3 Caps (Instrument 2017/510, made under s963BA, in force from 1 Jan 2018) — upfront: up to 60% of the policy cost in the first year for products issued from 1 Jan 2020 (80% for 2018 issues, 70% for 2019 issues). Ongoing: up to 20% of the policy cost in each later year. Client-initiated increases (a higher sum insured, a longer benefit period, extra cover, a change from stepped to level premiums, a shorter waiting period, a change from any to own occupation, or indemnity to agreed value): up to 60% of the annualised increase, then 20% from the anniversary. CPI increases aren't client-initiated, so only the 20% applies.
4 Level commission — there is no numeric cap; the condition is an identical benefit ratio every year. Don't quote a 'level commission cap'.
5 Clawback (instrument s6) — if the policy is cancelled or not continued, or the policy cost is reduced, in year 1: 100% of the first-year commission (pro-rated for reductions); in year 2: 60%; after 24 months: nothing. Year-2 ongoing commission isn't clawed back. A client-initiated increase reversed within 12 months is clawed back at 100%. There is no clawback on death, self-harm, age-out or administrative error, and risk-reduction changes such as stopping smoking are ignored.
6 Worked examples (from the instrument) — a $1,000 first-year premium allows up to $600 upfront; if the policy is cancelled in year 2, 60% × $600 = $360 is clawed back; a $1,200 year-2 premium that includes a $150 client-initiated increase allows up to $90 + $210 = $300.
7 GST — the caps are tested on the commission excluding GST. Where a commission includes GST, the GST isn't a 'benefit' for conflicted-remuneration purposes.
8 Informed consent (s963BB; in force for insurance issued or sold on or after 9 Jul 2025, when personal advice is given on life risk, general or consumer credit insurance; general advice only is exempt) — before the client consents, disclose: the insurer's name, if known; the commission rate as a percentage of the policy cost; how often and for how long it is paid, including renewals; the nature of any services; that the law requires the client's consent; and that the consent is irrevocable. Consent is in writing, or a written record of verbal consent is kept; the client gets a copy as soon as reasonably practicable; records are kept for at least 5 years (s1101C(3)). Information already in the SoA needn't be repeated if it is clearly identifiable. Consent covers renewals if the expected renewal periods were disclosed and the renewal rate and frequency don't exceed what was disclosed; otherwise new consent is needed. There is no annual re-consent for life risk commission. Without consent, the commission is conflicted remuneration, which can lead to civil penalties, banning orders or licence action.
9 Dates often misreported — the caps have applied since 1 Jan 2018 (60% from 1 Jan 2020), and consent since 9 Jul 2025, with no annual renewal for life risk. The instrument is due to sunset on 1 Oct 2027 unless it is remade; no remake had been announced at 23 Nov 2026.
10 Life Advice Guru practice — no advice fee for protection-only advice; commission shown in dollars in the SoA (s947B); written consent with the SoA. Example (Priya Natarajan, Corella Life, first-year policy cost $3,180): upfront 60% = $1,908; ongoing 20% = $636 a year from year 2 on a policy cost of $3,180, changing as the premium changes; amounts exclude GST.
limits: No commission on group super cover or default cover in super. Commission without the client's informed consent is prohibited. There is no numeric level-commission cap, so never quote one. Agents never let commission influence a comparison or recommendation, and Life Advice Guru never asks the client to pay a clawback.
evidenceRequired: Commission disclosure in the SoA: insurer, rate as a percentage of the policy cost, frequency and period including renewals, services, consent required and irrevocable
Client's written consent, or a written record of verbal consent
Copy of the consent given to the client
Consent record kept for at least 5 years
